candidates.name: Reasoning budget plus final output reservation
candidates.scope: typed allocation policy in Contract Runtime/Gateway plus protocol-specific adapter encoding
candidates.risk: medium-high because it changes an authority-critical model request boundary
candidates.compatibility: compatible only for routes with fresh verified enforcement capability; no provider-name branches
candidates.reason: Only this candidate directly prevents reasoning from consuming the reserved final region while preserving total tokens.

candidates.name: Contract output restructuring
candidates.risk: high; changes contract topology, merge authority and likely call count
candidates.compatibility: requires migration and can regress planning semantics
candidates.reason: It does not prevent each subcall's reasoning from exhausting its cap and violates the requested no-Prompt/no-contract-change boundary.

candidates.name: Fallback capability boundary
candidates.scope: exclude unknown or incapable routes from final-reservation-required contracts
candidates.risk: low narrative risk but availability can decrease
candidates.compatibility: safe and provider-independent when keyed by route fingerprint and typed capability
candidates.reason: It prevents another unsafe call but cannot produce the required artifact if no capable route exists; alone it is containment.

candidates.name: Force strict tool/JSON output or append a final-only continuation
candidates.scope: change structured mode or add a second request
candidates.risk: medium-high; thinking can still consume the cap and continuation changes retry/cost/prompt semantics
candidates.compatibility: the observed fallback was plain/stale and had no verified strict-tool capability
tests: continuation authority and duplicate artifact handling
candidates.reason: Neither forcing output shape nor adding a continuation guarantees reserved capacity, and both broaden the authorized behavior.

decision: Implement A only with C as a mandatory capability guard; do not implement B or D.
